mainTopic: עגלה ערופה and witnesses who contradict each other, why עגלה ערופה and the סוטה waters stopped, a ברייתא on society's decline, and the משנה's lines on אשכולות and the declaration of מעשר.
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's list of changes made by יוחנן כהן גדול, and then the גמרא explains the משנה's lines about עגלה ערופה. A ברייתא teaches that the ritual never frees a killer who is found later. If even one person knows who the killer is, or the judges saw the killing, the ritual is not done, so one witness is believed. The גמרא then works through cases where witnesses contradict each other: עולא and רבי יצחק change the משנה's wording, while רבי חייא keeps it and splits between witnesses who came together and witnesses who came one after the other. In the end the whole משנה is explained as dealing with invalid witnesses, following רבי נחמיה's rule to follow the majority, and the גמרא gives two versions of that rule. Next it explains why עגלה ערופה stopped when open murder spread, and why the bitter waters of סוטה stopped: they only work when the husband himself is clean of sin. A long ברייתא lists how one moral failing in society led to the next. The amud ends by explaining אשכולות and beginning the reason יוחנן כהן גדול cancelled the declaration of מעשר. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two more changes in the days of the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list: before his time hammers were heard in ירושלים, and in his days no one needed to ask about דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until his days, the hammer would strike in ירושלים. And in his days, there was no need to ask about דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes listing what changed in the days of יוחנן כהן גדול. It adds two last items: the banging of hammers in ירושלים, and the question of דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until his time, smiths would hammer in ירושלים on חול המועד, and he stopped it. In his days people were so careful to separate מעשרות that nobody had to ask whether produce had been tithed. This closes the משנה before the גמרא begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Hammer, here the hammer of the metalworkers.
Produce bought from someone who may not have separated מעשרות.

phrases.english: Until his days the hammer
would strike in Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: The smiths' hammers banging on חול המועד. He put a stop to it.

phrases.english: And in his days there was no need
to ask about doubtfully tithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַּטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the days of יוחנן כהן גדול, hammering in ירושלים on חול המועד was stopped, and everyone was careful with מעשרות, so there was no need to ask about דמאי.

steps.title: Breaking the heifer's neck does not free the killer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from a פסוק that if the killer is found after the עגלה ערופה, he is still punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How do we know that if the heifer's neck was already broken and then the killer was found, the ritual does not exempt him? The verse says: 'And the land shall not be atoned for the blood spilled in it, except by the blood of the one who spilled it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא about עגלה ערופה. It asks what happens if the killer turns up after the ritual was already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the heifer already brought atonement, so the killer is off the hook. The פסוק says the land is only atoned through the blood of the actual killer. So the עגלה ערופה never replaces punishing the killer once he is found.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where?' It asks for a source in the פסוקים.
The heifer's neck was broken, which is the עגלה ערופה ritual.
'The verse teaches.' This introduces the source.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that עגלה ערופה is a stand-in for an unknown killer. It is never a way out for a killer who is found.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught: From where is it derived
that if the heifer's neck was broken
and afterward the killer was found
that it does not exempt him?
The verse states:
"And the land shall not be atoned
for the blood that was spilled in it
except by the blood of the one who spilled it."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:33

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם נֶעֶרְפָה הָעֶגְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the עגלה ערופה part of the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the killer is found after the עגלה ערופה, he is not exempt. The land is atoned only through the killer's own blood.

steps.title: From the משנה: one witness is believed if no one contradicts him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and learns that a single witness who saw the killer is believed when no one contradicts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one witness says 'I saw the killer,' and another says he didn't, and they break the neck. The reason is that he is contradicted. But if no one contradicts him, one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and draws a lesson from what it leaves unsaid. It reasons that the neck is broken only because the witness was contradicted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, one witness saw the killer and a second denied it, so they break the neck. The גמרא reads this backwards. If nobody had contradicted him, his testimony alone would be enough to cancel the ritual. This is surprising, since we usually need two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is.' It introduces a precise reading of the text.

steps.confusionAlert: Normally the תורה requires two witnesses. Here one witness is enough because the issue is only whether the killer is 'known.'

phrases.english: One witness says
I saw the killer, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. The 'etc.' covers the second witness who says 'you did not see,' so they break the neck.

phrases.english: The reason is that he contradicts him,
but if he does not contradict him,
one witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, הָא לָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה about witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single uncontradicted witness who saw the killer is believed, and the heifer's neck is not broken.

steps.title: Where do we learn that one witness is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one witness is believed here.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of what it just learned. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually two witnesses are needed, so a rule trusting one witness needs a source. The גמרא is asking for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these things?' A request for the source of a rule.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a single uncontradicted witness cancels the עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: 'It is not known who struck him': if anyone knows, no ritual
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'it is not known who struck him' to teach that if even one person anywhere knows, the neck is not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: 'It is not known who struck him.' This means that if it is known who struck him, even by one person at the end of the world, they would not break the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the words of the פסוק exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ritual applies only when the killer is 'not known.' If even one person knows who did it, the killer is no longer 'not known,' so the condition for the ritual is missing. That is why one witness is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not known who struck him.' This is the condition for עגלה ערופה.
'At the end of the world.' Even someone very far away.
They break the neck of the heifer.

steps.whatToRemember: עגלה ערופה is only for a killer who is truly unknown. If even one person knows who it was, there is no ritual, so one witness is enough.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"It is not known who struck him."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:1

phrases.english: So if it was known who struck him,
even by one person at the end of the world,
they would not break the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא נוֹדַע מִי הִכָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires that the killer be unknown. If even one person knows, the condition is missing, so a single witness cancels the ritual.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: if the סנהדרין saw the killing, no ritual
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that if the סנהדרין saw a killing but did not recognize the killer, they still do not break the neck, because they cannot say 'our eyes did not see.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: How do we know that if the סנהדרין saw someone kill a person but do not recognize him, they would not break the neck? The verse says: 'And our eyes did not see.' But they did see!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי עקיבא, who adds a new case. Here the judges themselves saw the murder but cannot identify the killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that since the killer is still unidentified, the ritual should happen. But the elders must declare 'our eyes did not see,' and here that would be false. So seeing the act alone, even without knowing who it was, cancels the ritual.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And our eyes did not see.' Part of the elders' declaration.
'But didn't they see?' They could not truthfully make the declaration.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways the ritual is canceled. It is canceled if someone knows who the killer is, and also if the judges saw the killing even without recognizing him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: From where is it derived
that if the Sanhedrin saw someone
who killed a person
but they do not recognize him,
that they would not break the neck?
The verse states: "And our eyes did not see,"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:7

phrases.english: but did they not see?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְסַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁרָאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a further case where the ritual is canceled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the סנהדרין saw the killing, even without recognizing the killer, the heifer's neck is not broken, since they cannot say 'our eyes did not see.'

steps.title: How can one witness contradict a believed witness?
steps.stepSummary: If one witness is believed here, a second single witness should not be able to cancel him, because of עולא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said one witness is believed here, how can the other single witness contradict him? Didn't עולא say: wherever the תורה believes one witness, he counts as two, and one person's words cannot stand against two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's ruling that when one witness says 'I saw the killer' and another says 'you did not,' they still break the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 taught that one witness is believed here. עולא says such a believed witness has the strength of two witnesses. So the second witness is only one against 'two' and should not be able to cancel the first.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is as if there are two witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: עולא's rule is a general principle. It applies everywhere the Torah trusts one witness, not only to עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: Now that you have said one witness is believed,
phrases.notes: This points back to what the גמרא learned from the משנה in step 3.

phrases.aramaic: אִידַּךְ חַד הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: how can the other single one contradict him?
But didn't Ulla say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed one witness
here there are two,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם!
phrases.english: and the words of one have no standing against two!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ עֵד אֶחָד מְהֵימַן, אִידַּךְ חַד הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that one witness is believed and challenges the משנה's case where a second witness contradicts him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling 'they would break the neck' when one witness contradicts another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to עולא, a believed single witness counts as two. A lone contradicting witness should not be able to cancel him.

steps.title: עולא and רבי יצחק change the wording to 'they would not break the neck'
steps.stepSummary: עולא and רבי יצחק read the משנה as saying they do not break the neck in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא could say to you: read the משנה as 'they would not break the neck.' רבי יצחק also said: read it as 'they would not break the neck.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the משנה so it fits עולא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first witness is believed and the second cannot cancel him, the killer is considered known. So the neck is not broken. רבי יצחק agrees with this reading on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: They break the neck of the עגלה ערופה

phrases.english: Ulla could say to you,
teach: "They would not break the neck."
phrases.notes: He is changing the words of the משנה, which say 'they would break the neck.'

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Yitzchak,
teach: "They would not break the neck."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by changing the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says the neck is broken even though one witness is believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'they would not break the neck,' in line with עולא's rule.

steps.title: רבי חייא keeps the wording 'they would break the neck'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא holds the משנה should read 'they would break the neck.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא said: read it as 'they would break the neck.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא disagrees and keeps the משנה's ruling that the neck is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חייא, when two single witnesses contradict each other, the killer is not known. So the עגלה ערופה is brought. This sets up the question of how he deals with עולא's rule.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya said,
teach: "They would break the neck."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing reading to that of עולא and רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness contradicts another, they break the neck.

steps.title: רבי חייא seems to clash with עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי חייא's reading seems to go against עולא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חייא, עולא's rule is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא. How can he say the neck is broken, if a believed single witness counts as two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same problem raised in step 7, now aimed at רבי חייא, who did not change the wording. It sets up his answer in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Chiya, Ulla's rule is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge of step 7 against רבי חייא's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's reading 'they would break the neck'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא's rule says one witness against a believed witness has no standing. So the neck should not be broken.

steps.title: Together versus one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about witnesses who came at the same time. עולא is talking about witnesses who came one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, in the משנה, they came at the same time. There, in עולא's rule, they came one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי חייא by splitting the cases: same time versus one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both witnesses testify together, neither one was accepted first, so they cancel each other. Then the killer is unknown and the neck is broken. עולא's rule works only when the first witness was already accepted before the second came.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא does not reject עולא's rule. He limits it to witnesses who came one after the other.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here, at the same time,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case in the משנה.

phrases.english: there, one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּבַת אַחַת, כָּאן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against רבי חייא by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא's reading goes against עולא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about witnesses at the same time. עולא's rule is about witnesses one after the other.

steps.title: A challenge to רבי חייא from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when two witnesses contradict one, they break the neck. That suggests that one against one, they would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if one witness says 'I saw the killer' and two say 'you did not see,' they break the neck. This implies that one against one, they do not break the neck. This is a refutation of רבי חייא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a case in the משנה closely and draws an inference that seems to disprove רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically needs two witnesses to cancel the one. That suggests a single contradicting witness would not be enough, so the neck would not be broken. That is the opposite of רבי חייא's reading.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״רָאִיתִי אֶת הַהוֹרֵג״,
phrases.english: We learned: one witness says, "I saw the killer,"
and two say, "You did not see" — they would break the neck.

phrases.aramaic: הָא חַד וְחַד — לֹא הָיוּ עוֹרְפִין,
phrases.english: This implies one against one — they would not break the neck,
a refutation of Rabbi Chiya!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״רָאִיתִי אֶת הַהוֹרֵג״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new attack on רבי חייא, this time from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's reading 'they would break the neck' in a case of one against one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה needs two witnesses to cancel one. So one against one would not cancel, and the neck would not be broken.

steps.title: The end of the משנה gives the opposite inference
steps.stepSummary: Inferring from the end of the משנה would teach the opposite, so the inference from the first part proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, say the end of the משנה: if two say 'we saw' and one says 'you did not see,' they do not break the neck. This implies that one against one, they do break the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the refutation by showing that the same kind of inference from the end of the משנה points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we infer from the end of the משנה, one against one would mean they do break the neck. That is exactly רבי חייא's view. Since the two inferences cancel out, neither one can disprove רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
The end part of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: An inference from one part of a משנה cannot be used as proof when another part of the same משנה gives the opposite inference. So רבי חייא's view survives.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the end part:
two say, "We saw,"

phrases.aramaic: וְעֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״לֹא רְאִיתֶם״ — לֹא הָיוּ עוֹרְפִין.
phrases.english: and one witness says, "You did not see" — they would not break the neck.
This implies one against one — they would break the neck.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the inference in step 12, so the two cancel each other out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the refutation in step 12 by showing that the משנה's end gives the opposite inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof against רבי חייא from the first part of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same method of inference applied to the end of the משנה supports רבי חייא, so these inferences prove nothing.

steps.title: The whole משנה is about invalid witnesses, following רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation: the entire משנה deals with פסולי עדות, and it follows רבי נחמיה's rule to go after the majority of opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the whole משנה is about people who are not valid witnesses, and it follows רבי נחמיה. He says that wherever the תורה believes one witness, follow the majority of opinions. Two women against one man count like two men against one man.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier inference did not work, the גמרא offers a fresh way to read the whole משנה: it is talking about witnesses who are normally not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 assumed the משנה spoke of valid witnesses, so 'two against one' would be obvious and must be there only to imply something about one against one. Read instead as invalid witnesses such as women, 'two against one' is a real new rule from רבי נחמיה: follow the side with more people. So nothing can be implied about one against one, and the opposite inferences from the beginning and end of the משנה fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are normally not allowed to testify (such as women)
The majority of opinions (the side with more people)
The Torah believed a single witness
Rather (drops the earlier approach and gives a new one)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not repeating the obvious rule that two valid witnesses beat one. With invalid witnesses, 'two against one' is a new rule (follow the majority), so no lesson about one against one can be drawn from it.

phrases.english: Rather: the entire Mishnah is about people disqualified from testimony,
and it follows Rabbi Nechemya, who says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed a single witness,
follow the majority of opinions,
and they treated two women against one man
like two men against one man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 showed the inference proves nothing, this step gives a new reading of the entire משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (invalid witnesses) and tying it to a named תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was talking about valid witnesses, so its two-against-one cases seemed to be there only to imply rules about one against one, and those implied rules contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about invalid witnesses and follows רבי נחמיה's majority rule. Its cases teach that rule directly, so no inference about one against one can be drawn from them.

steps.title: Second version: a valid witness who came first outweighs any number of women
steps.stepSummary: Some report a different version: if one valid witness came first, even a hundred women count only as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: whenever a valid single witness came first, even a hundred women are considered like one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the rule. It limits how much weight women's testimony has against a valid witness who already testified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, once a valid witness has testified, any number of invalid witnesses together count only like one person. So they cannot outweigh him. This changes which cases the משנה can be talking about, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: A valid witness who came first

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד — כָּשֵׁר מֵעִיקָּרָא,
phrases.english: Wherever a single witness came, a valid one, at the outset,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה נָשִׁים כִּי אֶחָד דָּמְיָין.
phrases.english: even a hundred women are considered like one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the rule behind step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valid single witness who testified first cannot be outweighed by any number of women; together they count as one.

steps.title: In this version, the משנה is about a woman who came first
steps.stepSummary: According to the second version, the משנה must be describing a case where the first witness was a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case here? Where a woman came first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which case the משנה must be talking about according to the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a valid man had come first, the women after him could never outweigh him. So the משנה, which does let the majority decide, must be talking about a case where a woman testified first and other women came after her.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: And here, with what are we dealing?
Where a woman came at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the second version's rule to the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might have a valid man as the first witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first witness was a woman, so a majority of women can decide.

steps.title: Rewording רבי נחמיה's statement to fit the second version
steps.stepSummary: Under the second version, רבי נחמיה's words must read 'two women against one woman,' while two women against one man is evenly balanced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And reword רבי נחמיה like this: רבי נחמיה says: wherever the תורה believed one witness, follow the majority of opinions. Two women against one woman are like two men against one man. But two women against one man are like half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of רבי נחמיה's statement so that it matches the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said 'two women against one man.' Here it becomes 'two women against one woman,' since all the witnesses are the same kind. Two women against a valid man do not win; the two sides are evenly balanced.

phrases.english: And reword the statement of Rabbi Nechemya like this:
Rabbi Nechemya says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed a single witness,
follow the majority of opinions,
and they treated two women against one woman
like two men against one man,
but two women against one man
are like half against half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second version by changing the wording of רבי נחמיה's statement from step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נחמיה said two women against one man are like two against one.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said two women against one woman. Two women against one man are only evenly balanced.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need two cases of invalid witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה teaches the majority rule twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two cases of invalid witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. The משנה gives two cases (two against one each way), and both seem to teach the same majority rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the whole משנה is about invalid witnesses, both cases seem to teach one idea: follow the majority. The גמרא wants to know what the second case adds.

phrases.english: And two cases of invalid witnesses, why do I need them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question that applies to both readings of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the second case of invalid witnesses teaches.

steps.title: The majority rule works both to be strict and to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: Both cases are needed so we don't think the majority is followed only when it leads to a stricter result.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we follow the majority only to be strict, but not to be lenient. So the משנה teaches us that we follow it either way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: each case teaches something, because one leads to a strict result and the other to a lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the majority says the killer was not seen, the ritual must be done. That is the strict result. When the majority says he was seen, the ritual is skipped. That is the lenient result. Without both cases, we might think the majority counts only for the strict result.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: With invalid witnesses we follow the majority of opinions, whether that makes us do the עגלה ערופה ritual or skip it.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוֹב דֵּעוֹת — לְחוּמְרָא,
phrases.english: when we follow the majority of opinions, that is to be strict,
phrases.notes: Strict here means the ritual has to be performed.

phrases.english: but to be lenient, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two cases show that the majority rule applies both for strictness and for leniency.

steps.title: עגלה ערופה stopped when murderers multiplied
steps.stepSummary: Moving to the next line of the משנה, a ברייתא explains that עגלה ערופה was stopped because it applies only when the killer is unknown, and murderers began killing openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When murderers multiplied' and so on. The רבנן taught: when murderers multiplied, עגלה ערופה was stopped, because it only comes for a case of doubt. When murderers who killed openly multiplied, עגלה ערופה was stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עגלה ערופה is only done when nobody knows who the killer is. Once murderers were killing out in the open and people knew who they were, the cases no longer fit that rule, so the ritual stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: The ritual of the heifer whose neck is broken was stopped
For a case of doubt (the killer is unknown)

steps.whatToRemember: עגלה ערופה is only for an unknown killer. Once murder became open and common, the ritual stopped.

phrases.english: "When murderers multiplied," etc.
The Rabbis taught:
When murderers multiplied, the heifer whose neck is broken was stopped,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא עַל הַסָּפֵק.
phrases.english: because it comes only for a case of doubt.

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ הָרוֹצְחָנִין בְּגָלוּי — בָּטְלָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה.
phrases.english: When murderers acting openly multiplied, the heifer whose neck is broken was stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the witness discussion and opens the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עגלה ערופה was stopped once murderers acted openly, because the ritual only applies when the killer is unknown.

steps.title: The waters only test a wife when the husband is free of sin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said the bitter waters stopped once adulterers became common. A ברייתא explains why: the waters only work when the husband is clean of sin. It also brings a supporting פסוק from הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: once adulterers became many, the waters were stopped. The רבנן taught: the תורה says 'And the man shall be cleared of sin.' This means that when the husband is clean of sin, the waters test his wife. When the husband is not clean of sin, the waters do not test his wife. And another פסוק says: 'I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and quotes a ברייתא. The ברייתא explains that the waters of סוטה depend on the husband's own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the man shall be cleared of sin' is read as a condition: the waters work only if the husband himself is clean. So once many men were sinning, the waters stopped working, and the ritual was stopped. The ברייתא also adds a פסוק from הושע, and the next step asks why.

keyTerms.meaning: Adulterers, people who sin with a married woman
'And the man shall be cleared of sin' (a פסוק about סוטה)
The waters test (whether the wife sinned)
'And it says': brings an extra פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the waters were stopped only because people lost faith in them. The ברייתא says the waters simply do not work when the husband is not clean of sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's report that the ritual of the bitter waters ended: it depended on the moral level of the husbands.

phrases.english: From when the adulterers increased, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"And the man shall be cleared of sin"
phrases.notes: במדבר ה:לא

phrases.english: When the man is clean of sin —
the waters test his wife;
if the man is not clean of sin —
the waters do not test his wife.
And it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא אֶפְקוֹד עַל בְּנוֹתֵיכֶם כִּי תִזְנֶינָה כּוּ׳״.
phrases.english: "I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry, etc."
phrases.notes: הושע ד:יד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 explained the end of עגלה ערופה, this moves to the next line of the משנה, about the end of the bitter waters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bitter waters test a wife only when her husband is free of sin.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא add a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra פסוק from הושע adds beyond the תורה's own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a second פסוק. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule already seems clear from the תורה's words 'the man shall be cleared of sin.' So the extra פסוק must be teaching something more. The גמרא is about to show what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (here: what is the point of)

phrases.english: What is the point of "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second פסוק quoted at the end of the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the פסוק from הושע teach that the תורה's פסוק does not?

steps.title: The sins of the husband's children count too
steps.stepSummary: Without the second פסוק, we might think only the husband's own sin matters. The פסוק in הושע shows that the sins of his sons and daughters also stop the waters from working.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: his own sin, yes, it stops the waters; but the sin of his sons and daughters, no. Come and hear: 'I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: the פסוק in הושע widens the rule to include the sins of the husband's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'the man shall be cleared of sin' alone, we would think only the husband's personal sin counts. The פסוק in הושע speaks about daughters and daughters-in-law sinning, and says God will not punish the wives. That shows the waters also fail when the family's sins are present.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible mistake)

phrases.english: And if you would say: his own sin — yes,
that of his sons and daughters — no,
come and hear:
"I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry,
phrases.notes: He means: I won't punish your wives through the waters, because of what your daughters do.

phrases.english: nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with the first thing the second פסוק adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק teaches that the sins of the husband's sons and daughters also stop the waters from working.

steps.title: Sin with an unmarried woman counts too
steps.stepSummary: We might think only sin with a married woman stops the waters. The rest of the פסוק shows that sin with an unmarried woman also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you might say: the sin of a married woman, yes; the sin of an unmarried woman, no. Come and hear: 'For they go aside with harlots and sacrifice with prostitutes, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second thing the פסוק in הושע adds: even the sin of being with an unmarried woman (פנויה) stops the waters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think only the serious sin of אשת איש would matter. But the פסוק talks about men going with harlots, who are not married. So even that kind of sin makes the waters fail.
steps.whatToRemember: The waters fail when the husband is not clean: this includes his own sin, his children's sins, and even sin with an unmarried woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: עֲוֹן אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ — אִין,
phrases.english: And if you would say: the sin of a married woman — yes,
the sin of an unmarried woman — no,
come and hear:
"For they go aside with harlots,
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק in הושע ד:יד.

phrases.english: and sacrifice with prostitutes, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: עֲוֹן אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second thing the פסוק teaches, following the same pattern as step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that even sin with an unmarried woman stops the waters from working.

steps.title: What does the end of the פסוק mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the last words of the same פסוק in הושע: 'and a people without understanding will stumble.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and a people that does not understand will stumble' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last words of the פסוק and asks what they mean. This sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first parts of the פסוק were already used for the rule. Now the גמרא wants to know how the ending fits in, and the next step explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Will stumble, be troubled or confused

phrases.english: What is "And a people that does not understand will stumble"?
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the same פסוק in הושע ד:יד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier parts of the פסוק (steps 23–24) to its ending.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the closing words of the פסוק in הושע.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the waters work only if you keep yourselves clean
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the נביא told Israel: if you are careful about your own behavior, the waters test your wives; if not, they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The נביא said to ישראל: If you are careful about yourselves, the waters test your wives. And if not, the waters do not test your wives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question: the end of the פסוק is the נביא warning the people that the waters depend on the men's own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people who 'stumble' are the men who sin themselves and then find the waters no longer work on their wives. They are left confused and troubled, with no way to clear up their suspicion. This matches the rule of the ברייתא in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Careful and strict about your own behavior

steps.whatToRemember: The bitter waters of סוטה worked only when the husbands were clean of sin. Once adulterers became common, the waters stopped working, so the ritual was stopped.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The prophet said to Israel:
If you are careful about yourselves —
the waters test your wives,
and if not —
the waters do not test your wives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמַר לָהֶם נָבִיא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 and ties back to the rule of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the פסוק means the people will be troubled because the waters only test wives when the men are careful about their own behavior.

steps.title: When people who take benefits increased, justice fell apart
steps.stepSummary: Once many people accepted favors from others, judgments became twisted, behavior became corrupt, and there was no comfort in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that people who accept benefits from others became many, the laws became twisted, people's deeds became corrupt, and there was no peace of mind in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list of sayings in the style of the משנה. The first one says that when people who take favors increased, justice and behavior broke down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who accepts benefits feels he owes the giver something. When this spreads, especially among judges, rulings bend toward whoever gave the gift. The whole society then loses its sense of fairness and calm.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time that ... became many
People who accept benefits or favors from others

phrases.english: From the time that those who accept benefit became many,
phrases.notes: People who take favors from others, which makes them feel they owe something back.

phrases.english: the laws became twisted
and deeds became corrupted
and there was no comfort in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the סוטה waters and opens a new list of 'from the time that' sayings, in the same style as the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Widespread acceptance of favors leads to twisted judgments, corrupt behavior, and loss of peace.

steps.title: When judges showed favoritism, they traded God's yoke for man's
steps.stepSummary: Once judges started ruling based on who stood before them, the commands 'do not fear' and 'do not show favor' were no longer kept, and judges served people instead of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that judges who look at the faces of the people in court became many, 'You shall not fear' stopped being kept, and 'You shall not show favor' came to an end. They took off the yoke of Heaven and put on themselves the yoke of human beings.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with judges who decide cases based on who the people in court are. The גמרא says this cancels two commands from the תורה about judging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both commands come from the same פסוק in דברים: a judge must not be afraid of any person and must not favor anyone. A judge who looks at faces is worried about pleasing powerful people. So instead of answering to Heaven, he now answers to people.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges who 'look at faces,' meaning they favor certain people in court
'You shall not fear' (any person, when judging)
'You shall not recognize (show favor)' in judgment
The yoke of Heaven, accepting God's authority
The yoke of flesh and blood, being controlled by people

phrases.english: From the time that those who look at faces in judgment became many,
phrases.notes: These are judges who rule based on who the person is, not on the facts.

phrases.english: "You shall not fear" ceased,
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

phrases.english: and "You shall not show favor" came to an end,
and they threw off the yoke of Heaven
and placed upon themselves the yoke of flesh and blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second type of corrupt judging to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Favoritism in court cancels the commands 'do not fear' and 'do not show favor' and replaces loyalty to Heaven with loyalty to people.

steps.title: Whispering to judges drove away the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: Once people secretly whispered advice to judges, God's anger grew against Israel and the שכינה left, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that those who whisper whispers in court became many, great anger came upon Israel and the שכינה went away, because it says: 'In the midst of the judges He judges.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with people who secretly whisper to judges to push a ruling. The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that the שכינה rests with judges, so corrupt judging pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים says God stands among the judges. This means the שכינה is present when judges rule honestly. When judges are swayed by secret whispers, the שכינה leaves and God's anger takes its place.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who whisper whispers, secretly advising or pressuring judges

phrases.english: From the time that those who whisper whispers in judgment became many —
phrases.notes: People who quietly whisper to a judge to push the ruling their way.

phrases.english: fierce anger increased in Israel,
and the Divine Presence departed,
because it is stated:
"In the midst of the judges He judges."
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:1. Here אלהים means the judges, and God stands among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third kind of court corruption. This time a פסוק is brought as a source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Secret pressure on judges brings God's anger and makes the שכינה leave, since the שכינה rests among honest judges.

steps.title: Greed leads to calling evil good, which leads to cries of woe
steps.stepSummary: A chain reaction: when people followed their greed, people who call evil good increased. When those increased, cries of 'woe' filled the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that people whose 'heart follows their greed' became many, 'those who say of evil that it is good and of good that it is evil' became many. From the time that 'those who say of evil that it is good and of good that it is evil' became many, cries of 'Woe, woe' became many in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a two-link chain using words from פסוקים. Greed leads to twisted values, and twisted values lead to suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person driven by greed will praise whoever benefits him, even a wicked person. So greed creates people who call evil good. The פסוק in ישעיהו that describes them begins with 'הוי' (woe), so the result is a world full of troubles and cries.

keyTerms.meaning: Their greed, their desire for gain
Woe, a cry of pain or trouble

phrases.english: From the time that "their heart goes after their greed" became many —
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 33:31

phrases.english: "those who say of evil, good, and of good, evil" became many.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:20

phrases.english: From the time that "those who say of evil, good, and of good, evil" became many —
cries of "Woe, woe" became many in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from specific court corruption to a general chain of moral decline.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greed produces people who call evil good, and that brings widespread suffering.

steps.title: Arrogant show-offs increased, and real students decreased
steps.stepSummary: When people who show off by spitting increased, arrogant people increased, students decreased, and the תורה had to go looking for people to learn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that people who draw out their spit became many, arrogant people became many, students became few, and the תורה goes around looking for people to learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The list turns from judges to arrogance. Showing off leads to more arrogant people and fewer real learners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing out spit was a way of acting important and looking down on others. Arrogant people feel they have nothing left to learn, so fewer people become students. The תורה is pictured as wandering around, looking for anyone who will learn it.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who draw out their spit, a show-off gesture of arrogance
Goes around looking for people who will learn it

phrases.english: From the time that those who draw out spit became many —
phrases.notes: A way of acting important and showing that you look down on others.

phrases.english: arrogant people became many
and students became few,
and the Torah goes around looking for those who will learn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts the list from corruption in judging to arrogance and its effect on תורה learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arrogance spreads, real learners become fewer, and the תורה is left without people seeking it.

steps.title: Women began marrying arrogant men because people judge by appearance
steps.stepSummary: Once arrogant people increased, Jewish women started marrying them, because the generation looks only at the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time that arrogant people became many, the daughters of Israel began to marry arrogant men, because our generation looks only at the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last saying in the list. It says women began choosing arrogant husbands because people judge only by how someone appears. It also sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An arrogant man looks impressive from the outside. A generation that cares only about appearances will be drawn to him and ignore what he is like inside. This claim is about to be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of Israel, Jewish women
Looks only at the face, meaning only at outward appearance

phrases.english: From the time that arrogant people became many —
the daughters of Israel began to marry arrogant men,
because our generation looks only at the face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain from step 31: the increase of arrogant people leads to women marrying them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the generation judges by appearance, women began marrying arrogant men.

steps.title: Challenge: arrogant people are not even accepted at home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how women could want arrogant men, since a teaching says an arrogant person is not even accepted by his own household.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But the Master said: a person who acts arrogantly is not accepted even by the people of his own house, as it says: 'An arrogant man will not abide.' This means he will not be accepted even in his own home!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 32. If arrogant men are not even accepted by their own families, why would women choose to marry them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is based on a פסוק in חבקוק. The word 'ינוה' is read as connected to 'נוה,' meaning home. So the arrogant man is not wanted even in his own home, which seems to contradict the claim that women are drawn to him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' A word the גמרא uses to open a challenge
'But didn't the Master say...' bringing a teaching that contradicts

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't the Master say:
This one who acts arrogantly —
is not accepted even by the people of his own house,
as it is stated: "An arrogant man, and he will not abide,"
phrases.notes: חבקוק 2:5

phrases.english: "he will not abide" — even in his own home!
phrases.notes: A play on words: יִנְוֶה sounds like נָוֶה, which means home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 32 by bringing a contradicting teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that Jewish women began marrying arrogant men (step 32).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an arrogant man is rejected even by his own household, based on חבקוק 2:5, it makes no sense that women would choose to marry him.

steps.title: At first she is attracted, later he loses value in her eyes
steps.stepSummary: Both statements are true at different times. At first the woman jumps to marry him, but in the end he becomes cheap in her eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning she jumps at him. In the end he becomes worthless in their eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the timeline. The attraction happens before the marriage, and the rejection happens after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before marriage, she sees only his impressive outside, so she wants him, which fits step 32. Once she lives with him and sees who he really is, he loses value in her eyes, which fits the teaching that he is not accepted at home. So the two statements do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: She jumps at him (eager to marry him)

steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance looks impressive from far away, which is why a generation that judges by appearance is drawn to it. Up close, though, the arrogant person is not respected, even in his own home.

phrases.english: At first, she jumps at him,
in the end, he becomes cheap in their eyes.
phrases.notes: Literally 'on them,' meaning the women who married him, or his household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 33 by showing that each statement describes a different stage.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: before the marriage compared with after the marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that being drawn to an arrogant man and rejecting him at home could not both be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are attracted to an arrogant man at first, based on how he looks, but once they know him he loses his value. So both teachings are true.

steps.title: Judges paid by homeowners led to bribery
steps.stepSummary: When judges made homeowners give them business profits, bribery and twisted judgment increased, and goodness stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once more people forced homeowners to hand over business profits, bribery and twisted judgment grew, and goodness stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its chain of decline. Judges who depended on homeowners for money became open to bribery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first names the cause: judges were being supported by the people who came before them. Then it gives the result. A judge who takes money from the people he judges cannot stay fair.

keyTerms.meaning: those who place merchandise or profits on others

phrases.english: From when those who placed merchandise increased
phrases.notes: Judges who made people give them business profits to support them.

phrases.english: upon homeowners
bribery and the twisting of judgment increased,
and good ceased.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ מַטִּילֵי מְלַאי עַל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of declines
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judges who depend on the people they judge lead to bribery and corrupt judgment.

steps.title: Leaders owing favors led to everyone doing as he pleased
steps.stepSummary: When leaders said 'I accept your favor,' each person did what was right in his own eyes. The lowly rose, the lofty fell, and the kingdom declined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once there were more leaders who said 'I accept your favor' and 'I hold your favor,' it became common for each man to do what was right in his own eyes. Lowly people were raised, lofty people were lowered, and the kingdom kept getting worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says that once leaders owed favors, no one judged honestly. People did whatever they wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge who owes someone a favor cannot correct him. So there was no real authority, and everyone followed his own judgment. The social order flipped, and the government grew weaker.

phrases.english: From when 'I accept your favor' increased
phrases.notes: These are the words of judges who owe someone a favor.

phrases.english: and 'I hold your favors,'
'every man does what is right in his eyes' increased.
phrases.notes: שופטים 17:6

phrases.english: Lowly ones were raised, and lofty ones were lowered,
and the kingdom keeps declining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain of decline
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaders who owe favors lose their authority, and lawlessness follows.

steps.title: Misers led to people refusing to lend
steps.stepSummary: When stingy and greedy people increased, people hardened their hearts and refused to lend, breaking a פסוק in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once stingy and greedy people increased, people with hard hearts who closed their hands and would not lend also increased. They broke what is written in the תורה: 'Guard yourself in case' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says greed led people to stop lending to the poor. That is against a clear פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stinginess spread from a few people to society as a whole. The ברייתא shows this is not only bad behavior. It breaks the תורה's command not to hold back a loan from a poor person.

phrases.english: From when misers and those greedy for profit increased,
those who harden the heart increased
and those who close their hands from lending,
and they transgressed what is written in the תורה:
'Guard yourself in case' and so on.
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9. The פסוק warns against refusing a loan to a poor person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain of decline
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greed led people to refuse loans, breaking a תורה command.

steps.title: Immodesty increased, then stopped, the bitter waters
steps.stepSummary: When immodest women increased, the testing of a סוטה with the bitter waters increased, but in the end it stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once women with 'stretched-out necks and flirting eyes' increased, use of the bitter waters increased. But then the waters stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ties this back to the topic of the מסכתא, the סוטה. More immodesty first meant more women were tested with the bitter waters, until the testing stopped completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, the bitter waters were used more because more women were suspected. When immorality became too common, the waters stopped working, so the practice ended.

keyTerms.meaning: the bitter waters of a סוטה

phrases.english: From when women with 'stretched-out necks and flirting eyes' increased,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:16

phrases.english: the bitter waters increased,
but then they ceased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain of decline
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immodesty first increased the use of the bitter waters, and later brought it to an end.

steps.title: Taking gifts shortens life
steps.stepSummary: When people who take gifts increased, lives became shorter, as the פסוק says, 'He who hates gifts will live.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Once more people accepted gifts, days became fewer and years became shorter, as it is written: 'And he who hates gifts will live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says taking gifts shortens a person's life. It proves this from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises life to someone who hates gifts. The ברייתא reads the reverse into it: someone who loves taking gifts loses years.

keyTerms.meaning: and he who hates gifts will live

phrases.english: From when those who accept gifts increased,
the days decreased and the years were shortened,
as it is written: 'And he who hates gifts will live.'
phrases.notes: משלי 15:27

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain of decline, with a פסוק as support
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting gifts shortens life.

steps.title: Arrogance led to disputes
steps.stepSummary: When arrogant people increased, arguments in ישראל increased.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once people with puffed-up hearts increased, disputes in ישראל increased.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says pride causes arguments. A proud person will not back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next line, which also ends with 'disputes increased.' Here the cause is a bad character trait. In the next line the cause is not learning enough.

phrases.english: From when those with puffed-up hearts increased,
disputes in ישראל increased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain of decline
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arrogance causes disputes.

steps.title: Students who did not learn enough split the תורה
steps.stepSummary: When students of שמאי and הלל did not serve their teachers enough, disputes grew and the תורה became like two תורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once there were more students of שמאי and הלל who did not serve their teachers as much as they needed to, disputes in ישראל increased, and the תורה became like two תורות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains where the many arguments between בית שמאי and בית הלל came from. Students did not spend enough time with their teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cause is not bad intentions. It is missing knowledge. Students who did not fully learn from their teachers came to different conclusions. So the halacha seemed to split into two systems.

keyTerms.meaning: served their teachers, learned by being with them

phrases.english: From when students of שמאי and הלל increased
who did not serve their teachers as much as they needed,
disputes in ישראל increased,
and the תורה became like two תורות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second cause for disputes, alongside arrogance
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not spending enough time learning from one's teachers leads to splits in halacha.

steps.title: Taking charity from non-Jews brought ישראל down
steps.stepSummary: When people took charity from non-Jews, ישראל fell low. The ברייתא says this in a polite, reversed way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once more people accepted charity from non-Jews, ישראל was 'above' and they were 'below,' ישראל was 'in front' and they were 'behind.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא's chain. Depending on non-Jews for charity lowered ישראל's standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words sound like ישראל was on top. But the meaning is the opposite: ישראל was below and behind. The ברייתא did not want to say something bad about ישראל openly.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a good result. It is a polite way of saying that ישראל ended up below and behind.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's whole list shows that one bad trait in society pulls the next one along, from corrupt judges all the way to dependence on others.

phrases.english: From when those who accept charity from a non-Jew increased,
ישראל was above and they were below,
phrases.notes: Read this the other way around: ישראל ended up below. It's said politely so as not to speak badly of ישראל.

phrases.english: ישראל in front and they behind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final link in the ברייתא's chain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Depending on non-Jews for charity lowers ישראל's standing.

steps.title: What does 'clusters' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about יוסי בן יועזר and asks what אשכולות means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When יוסי בן יועזר died...' What does 'clusters' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks the meaning of one word. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the אשכולות stopped when יוסי בן יועזר died. The word literally means grape clusters. The גמרא asks what it means when said about people.

keyTerms.meaning: an early sage named in the משנה

phrases.english: When יוסי בן יועזר died, etc.
What are 'clusters'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to explain the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אשכולות in the משנה

steps.title: A 'cluster' is a man who has everything
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that an אשכול is a man who has everything in him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it means a man who has everything in him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A 'cluster' is a complete person who has everything in him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אשכול is read as איש שהכל בו, 'a man who contains everything.' Like a cluster full of grapes, such a person is full of every good quality.

keyTerms.meaning: a man who has everything in him

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
A man who has everything in him.
phrases.notes: The word אשכול is read as if it were איש שהכל בו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 43
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אשכול is a person who has everything in him.

steps.title: Why did יוחנן כהן גדול stop the declaration of מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why יוחנן כהן גדול cancelled the הודיית המעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: יוחנן כהן גדול did away with the declaration of the מעשר, etc. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and asks for the reason behind it. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הודיית המעשר is a statement in which a person declares that he gave all his מעשרות properly. The גמרא wants to know why a כהן גדול would stop people from saying it.

keyTerms.meaning: the declaration that one's מעשרות were given properly

phrases.english: יוחנן the High Priest
did away with the declaration of the מעשר, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֶעֱבִיר הוֹדָיַית הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason יוחנן כהן גדול cancelled the הודיית המעשר

steps.title: Because the מעשר was not given properly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that people were not giving the מעשר the right way, since the תורה says to give it to the לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: because they were not giving it the proper way. The Merciful One said that they should give it to the לוים,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason. People were not giving the מעשר the way the תורה requires. It begins to explain how, and the explanation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can't declare that he gave his מעשר properly if he really didn't. So the declaration was cancelled. The problem is that the תורה says the מעשר goes to the לוים, and the next lines will show what people were doing instead.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The גמרא keeps explaining in the next part.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said:
Because they were not giving it the proper way.
For the Merciful One said
that they should give it to the לוים,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין נוֹתְנִין אוֹתוֹ כְּתִיקּוּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 45
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The declaration was cancelled because people were not giving the מעשר to the לוים as the תורה commands.
